interface.signature: def criticalConnections(V: int, adj: List[List[int]]) -> List[List[int]]

preconditions.expression: V >= 1 and all(0 <= u < V for edge in adj for u in edge)
preconditions.description: V is a positive integer, and all nodes in adjacency list edges are valid vertex indices (0 ≤ u < V).
The graph is connected (no isolated vertices).

preconditions.expression: all(u < v or (u == v and False) for u in range(V) for v in adj[u])
preconditions.description: Each edge is represented exactly once in sorted order (u ≤ v) in the adjacency list.

postconditions.expression: all(len(edge) == 2 and edge[0] < edge[1] for edge in return_value)
postconditions.description: Each critical connection is represented as a sorted pair of vertices (u, v) where u < v.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= u < V and 0 <= v < V for edge in return_value for u, v in [edge])
postconditions.description: All vertices in the returned edges are valid vertex indices (0 ≤ u, v < V).

postconditions.expression: all(edge in [(u, v) for u in range(V) for v in adj[u] if u < v] for edge in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every returned edge exists in the input graph (as a sorted pair).

postconditions.expression: all(any((u, v) in return_value or (v, u) in return_value for u, v in [(x, y) for x in range(V) for y in adj[x] if x < y]) for u, v in return_value)
postconditions.description: The returned edges are exactly those whose removal disconnects the graph (critical connections).
The returned list of edges is sorted lexicographically.
